title: On Calculating the cost to the last penny
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：calculate　|　正文 360 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 calculate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the engineer ① calculated the cost to the last penny year after year, and every worker in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the engineer ② calculates the cost to the last penny for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ calculate the cost to the last penny at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ calculated the cost to the last penny before — a line in the manual for April 1962 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Calculating the cost to the last penny year after year, the engineer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ calculate how many days were left for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Calculate how many days were left at once and never mention it again.

By 1975 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the manual, and a new worker from the next workshop ⑧ calculates how many days were left year after year every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ calculated the cost to the last penny again when nobody else would.

⑩ To calculate the cost to the last penny, my mother said in 1980, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody calculates the cost to the last penny for the whole place again and somebody must calculate the cost to the last penny year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 计算（一般过去式 calculated the cost to the last penny：1968 年工程师头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 计算（一般现在 calculates the cost to the last penny：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 计算（不定式 to calculate the cost to the last penny：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 计算（过去完成时 had calculated the cost to the last penny：1962 年四月的说明书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 计算（动名词 calculating the cost to the last penny 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 估算（calculate how many days were left：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去估算还剩多少天）
G. v. 估算（calculate how many days were left：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 计算（后段两处：新来的工人照例 calculates how many days were left，而母亲又一次 calculated the cost to the last penny）

answers.why: calculate 意为“计算”，1968 年工程师年年地计算把费用算到最后一个便士，那是车间里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 calculated。
calculate 意为“计算”，自那以后工程师替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 calculates。
calculate 意为“计算”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯计算把费用算到最后一个便士”，此处为不定式 to calculate the cost to the last penny。
calculate 意为“计算”，说明书里 四月 那行字说明早在 1975 年之前就有人计算过，故用过去完成时 had calculated。
calculate 意为“计算”，工程师说“计算把费用算到最后一个便士这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 calculating the cost to the last penny 作主语。
calculate 意为“估算”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去估算还剩多少天”，should ever 之后用原形 calculate how many days were left。
calculate 意为“估算”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻估算还剩多少天（calculate how many days were left at once），以后再也不要提起。
calculate 意为“计算”，新来的工人每个年头都照例估算还剩多少天，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 calculates。
calculate 意为“计算”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地计算把费用算到最后一个便士，用一般过去式 calculated 叙述。
calculate 意为“计算”，结尾那句是母亲 1980 年的话：要计算把费用算到最后一个便士，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车间记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 calculate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the engineer calculated the cost to the last penny year after year, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the engineer calculates the cost to the last penny for the whole place whenever the workshop asks.
Calculating the cost to the last penny year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever calculate how many days were left for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next workshop calculates how many days were left year after year every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother calculated the cost to the last penny again, and the workshop remembered that half.
